# /data

Nothing here is committed (see the root `.gitignore`) — everything is either
generated or downloaded.

## Generated by the pipeline

| File | Produced by | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `synthetic_transactions.json` | `data_generator.py` | Main demo dataset |
| `ground_truth.json` | `data_generator.py` | Which wallets were deliberately planted |
| `graph.json` | `graph_builder.py` | Serialized graph, for inspecting without Python |

## Real data — the Elliptic Data Set

Two of the three Elliptic files are used, and both download without a login:

```bash
cd data
curl -L -o elliptic_txs_classes.csv \
  https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/ehowang/aml_project/main/data/elliptic_txs_classes.csv
curl -L -o elliptic_txs_edgelist.csv \
  https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/ehowang/aml_project/main/data/elliptic_txs_edgelist.csv
```

Verify you got the real thing before trusting any number computed from it:

| File | Rows | Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `elliptic_txs_classes.csv` | 203,769 | 4,545 class `1` (illicit), 42,019 class `2` (licit) |
| `elliptic_txs_edgelist.csv` | 234,355 | every endpoint appears in the classes file |

Those counts match the published dataset exactly. `python -m app.services.elliptic_real`
re-checks them on load and refuses to run on anything else.

### The third file

`elliptic_txs_features.csv` holds 166 anonymised columns and is **658 MB** (not
the ~200 MB usually quoted — that is the figure for a compressed copy). Every
mirror reachable from here truncates it partway; the best run reached 83 MB of
658 at roughly 92 KB/s, so it is **not used**.
It is also the file that carries the time-step column, which is why the
benchmark uses a component-grouped split rather than the paper's temporal one.

If you obtain it (Kaggle, "Elliptic Data Set", needs a login), the useful next
experiment is a head-to-head: our six structural features against Elliptic's
166, on the same split. That measures exactly how much signal our feature
engineering is missing.

### BitcoinHeist

The UCI BitcoinHeist ransomware dataset (real addresses, real ransomware
family labels) was also attempted. Its 111 MB archive truncates on every
download from `archive.ics.uci.edu` here, and the server supports neither
range requests nor resume, so it could not be used. Worth retrying on a
machine with a better connection — it is address-level, which matches our
wallet-scoring frame more closely than Elliptic's transaction-level data.
